name: Arodi
title: Son of Gad and ancestor of the Arodites
summary: Arodi was one of the seven sons of Gad, who was the son of Jacob and Zilpah. He is mentioned among those who went down to Egypt with Jacob's family during the famine in Canaan. Arodi became the ancestor of the clan of the Arodites among Gad's descendants. In Numbers, he is referred to by the shorter name form Arod, where his clan is counted among Gad's families in the census on the plains of Moab.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned among the descendants of Jacob
keyEvents.description: Arodi is listed as one of the seven sons of Gad in the record of Jacob's family that went down to Egypt.

keyEvents.title: The Journey to Egypt
keyEvents.description: Arodi was among the members of Jacob's household who traveled down to Egypt during the famine, where Joseph had already been placed in a position of power.

keyEvents.title: The Genealogy of the Arodites in the Census
keyEvents.description: In the book of Numbers, the genealogy of the Arodites is mentioned as one of the clans descended from Gad, during the census on the plains of Moab. Here, the shorter form of the name, Arod, is used.

versions.summary: Arodi was one of the sons of Gad, who was a son of Jacob. He is mentioned among those who went down to Egypt with Jacob's family. He became the ancestor of the clan of the Arodites among the descendants of Gad.
versions.title: Son of Gad
versions.reason: [major] 1 Chronicles 5:15–16 lists descendants of Gad, but Arodi is not specifically mentioned there. This reference is misleading and should be removed since it does not directly mention Arodi or his lineage in an identifiable way.; [minor] The role 'patriarch' is somewhat exaggerated for a person only mentioned in genealogies. 'Ancestor' or 'clan head' would be more precise, as he is primarily known as the forefather of the Arodite clan.; [minor] The lifespan 'c. 1850 BC' is difficult to verify. The chronology of the patriarchs varies greatly among different traditions. A broader range such as 'c. 1800–1700 BC' may be more defensible, but there is considerable uncertainty regardless.; [minor] Footnotes are missing. Information should be added about the name variation Arodi/Arod between Genesis and Numbers, as well as the linguistic background of the name.

footnotes.text: The name Arodi (Hebrew: אֲרוֹדִי) appears in Genesis 46:16, while the shorter form Arod (אֲרוֹד) is used in Numbers 26:17. Such variations in names are common in biblical genealogies and may result from different transmission traditions or abbreviations over time.

According to tradition, the tribe of Gad was allotted lands east of the Jordan (Transjordan), an area known for pastureland and suitable for cattle raising. As the ancestor of the clan of the Arodites, Arodi would thus have been connected to this region.

The number 70 people who went down to Egypt (Gen 46:27) has symbolic significance in Jewish tradition and represents completeness. Rabbinic sources discuss exactly who was included in this count, and some traditions count differently.
